title: What If the Earth Were Actually Flat? It Would Last About an Hour

scenes.text: What if the Earth were actually flat? You'd have about an hour to enjoy it.
Gravity pulls toward the centre. At the middle it points down. Near the edge it tilts inward, like climbing a steeper and steeper hill.
The air rushes toward the centre in violent storms. The oceans follow, pooling into one deep sea over 800 kilometres in radius.
No spinning iron core means no magnetic field. The solar wind starts stripping the air away, the way it did on Mars.
No plate tectonics either. No new mountains, and erosion slowly wears everything flat for real.
But it never gets that far. Gravity crushes the disc back into a ball within about an hour, with the energy of the whole planet turning to TNT. The sphere wins.

description:
What if the Earth were flat? Physicists told Gizmodo that gravity on a disc would point straight down only at the centre and tilt increasingly toward the middle near the edge, so air would rush inward in violent storms and the oceans would pool into a central sea roughly 863 km in radius.
Columbia University geophysicist James Davis notes a flat Earth could not generate a magnetic field, leaving the atmosphere to be stripped by the solar wind as on Mars, and could not explain plate tectonics, GPS or seasons. Caltech planetary scientist Dave Stevenson calculates that gravity would pull a flat Earth back into a sphere in about an hour, releasing energy comparable to converting the entire planet into TNT.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: The Sun is more than 100 times wider than Earth, so a flat-Earth sun circling overhead would have to be smaller than the planet itself. What's the next myth we should run through?
